items.title: Tune the RBF gamma of the kernel ridge member
items.spec: In base_predict the RBF kernel on z-scored descriptors uses a fixed gamma = 1/(2*n_desc). After the existing (lam, wr) grid search has picked its best pair, add a second, coordinate-wise step: with lam and wr fixed, evaluate gamma multipliers (0.5, 2.0) times the default using the same 4-fold GroupKFold inner loop, and keep the multiplier with the lowest summed absolute error (default 1.0 if neither beats it). Compute the squared-distance matrix once and reuse it for all gammas, so only the exp and the solves are repeated. Use the chosen gamma for the final fit and for the test kernel. This adds only 2 configs to the 9 already run, so runtime stays within the limit.

items.title: Rank-gauss transform of descriptors for the RBF kernel
items.spec: The kernel ridge member z-scores the clipped RDKit descriptors before the RBF kernel, but many descriptors are heavily skewed or are small integer counts, so Euclidean distance is dominated by a few columns. In base_predict, replace the mean/std standardisation of Za and Zb with a rank-based normal transform fitted on Za only: sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(500, len(Za)), random_state=seed), fit on Za, applied to both Za and Zb. Then drop columns whose transformed std on Za is below 1e-6, and set gamma = 1/(2*number of kept columns). Leave the tree learners' inputs and everything else unchanged.

items.title: Higher-resolution ECFP for the Tanimoto kernel only
items.spec: The Tanimoto kernel uses the same 1024-bit radius-2 ECFP as the trees, where bit collisions blur similarity. Compute a separate fingerprint used only by the kernel member: Morgan radius 3, fpSize 4096, bit vector, as float32. In fit_predict build Ktr_fp and Kte_fp from it and pass these as Fa/Fb to base_predict in place of the current Ftr[:, :N_BITS] slices. The tree learners keep the existing 1024-bit ECFP+FCFP plus descriptor matrix unchanged. Keep the matrices float32 for the dot product and cast the kernel to float64 before the solves, to keep time and memory low.

items.title: Similarity-gated meta-learner
items.spec: The ridge meta-learner uses one global weight per base learner, but kernel ridge is more reliable for molecules close to the training set and trees for distant ones. Let base_predict also return, for each row of Xb, s = the maximum Tanimoto similarity to the rows of Fa (already available from tanimoto(Fb, Fa)). In fit_predict collect s for out-of-fold rows and for the test rows. Build meta features [p_rf, p_lgb, p_krr, (s-0.5)*p_rf, (s-0.5)*p_lgb, (s-0.5)*p_krr] and fit Ridge(alpha=1.0) without the positive constraint (with intercept) on the out-of-fold rows; predict on the test rows with the same construction. Everything else stays the same.

items.title: ExtraTrees instead of random forest in the stack
items.spec: Replace the RandomForestRegressor base learner in base_predict with sklearn ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed), same inputs and same column position in the stack output. Extra-trees use random split thresholds, which is faster per tree and gives predictions less correlated with the LightGBM member than a random forest does, so the ridge meta-learner has more diversity to work with. No other change.

items.title: Add a linear descriptor kernel term to the kernel ridge member
items.spec: Lipophilicity has a strong roughly linear dependence on a few descriptors (logP-like terms) that the RBF kernel only captures locally. In base_predict add a third kernel term to the kernel ridge member: L = Za @ Zb.T / n_desc on the z-scored descriptors, so the full kernel is Tanimoto + wr*RBF + wl*L. Keep the existing (lam, wr) grid search with wl fixed at 0.1, then, with the chosen lam and wr, compare wl in (0.0, 0.1, 0.5) on the same 4-fold GroupKFold inner loop and keep the best. Use the selected wl in the final solve and in the test kernel. This adds 2 extra configs to the current 9.

items.title: Weight descriptors in the RBF kernel by forest importance
items.spec: The RBF kernel treats all ~210 z-scored descriptors equally although most are irrelevant to lipophilicity. In base_predict the random forest is already fitted on Xa before the kernel member; take rf.feature_importances_ for the descriptor columns (the last columns, from index 2*N_BITS), normalise them to mean 1 over the descriptor block, and multiply each z-scored column of Za and Zb by sqrt(importance + 0.05) before computing the RBF kernel (gamma unchanged). This gives an automatic-relevance-style metric at no extra fitting cost. The forest, LightGBM and the Tanimoto part stay unchanged.

items.title: Average fold-model test predictions with the full-fit prediction
items.spec: In fit_predict the five stacking-fold calls to base_predict fit base learners on 80% of the data and are used only for out-of-fold predictions. Make them also predict the test set: extend base_predict to accept an optional second prediction matrix pair (Xc, Fc) and return predictions for it from the same fitted models (no refitting, compute the extra kernel block once). In fit_predict average the five fold-model test prediction matrices, then average that with the full-data base_te (weight 0.5 each) before applying the meta-learner. This is a nearly free bagging step that lowers the variance of all three base learners.

items.title: Laplacian kernel on descriptors instead of RBF
items.spec: In the kernel ridge member replace the RBF kernel on z-scored descriptors with a Laplacian kernel: K = exp(-gamma * L1 distance), where the L1 distance is computed with scipy.spatial.distance.cdist(A, B, metric='cityblock') and gamma = 1/n_desc (n_desc = number of descriptor columns). The Laplacian kernel is less sensitive to single outlying descriptor values and usually suits tabular chemical descriptors better than the Gaussian one. Compute the train-train distance matrix once per base_predict call and reuse it across the (lam, wr) grid. Tanimoto part, grid and meta-learner stay unchanged.

items.title: Descriptor-only forest as the third view
items.spec: All three base learners see overlapping inputs; the random forest uses the full fingerprint+descriptor matrix, like LightGBM. Change only the forest in base_predict so that it is trained on the descriptor block alone (columns from 2*N_BITS onward of Xa and Xb), with RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.33, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). With ~210 dense columns instead of ~2260 mostly sparse ones the forest is faster and its errors are less correlated with the fingerprint-driven LightGBM and Tanimoto members, which should help the ridge meta-learner. No other change.

items.title: Ionization SMARTS count features
items.spec: logD at pH 7.4 depends strongly on charge state, which Morgan bits and the RDKit descriptors capture only loosely. Add a small block of hand-written SMARTS match counts computed in desc_vector, appended to the cached descriptor vector so they flow into the trees and the RBF kernel automatically. Use about 15-20 patterns: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, sulfonic/phosphonic acid, phenol, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amine (excluding amides, anilines, sulfonamides), amidine, guanidine, pyridine-like aromatic N, imidazole, aniline N, quaternary N, plus two summaries: total acidic groups and total basic groups, and a zwitterion flag (both > 0). Compile the SMARTS once at module level. Keep everything else unchanged.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy for both the ECFP and FCFP generators, so features are substructure counts rather than bits. For the Tanimoto kernel, switch the tanimoto function to the MinMax (generalised Tanimoto) form on the ECFP counts: sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)). Compute it in row chunks to keep memory under control, e.g. via min = (a + b - |a - b|) / 2 with chunks of about 200 rows, or use the cheaper dot-product form dot / (|a|^2 + |b|^2 - dot), which is also valid for counts and needs no code change. Prefer the dot-product form if runtime is a concern. Nothing else changes.

items.title: LightGBM huber/L2 objective instead of L1
items.spec: The LightGBM base learner uses objective='regression_l1', whose gradients are sign-only and usually fit small noisy datasets worse than a smooth loss, even when the metric is MAE. In lgb_params change the objective to 'huber' with alpha=1.0 (logD units), keeping learning_rate 0.03 and 600 rounds. Also add lambda_l2=1.0 and bagging_fraction=0.8 with bagging_freq=1 for mild regularisation. Leave the RF, KRR and meta-learner untouched.

items.title: Add CatBoost as a fourth base learner
items.spec: In base_predict, add a CatBoostRegressor trained on the same Xa (fingerprints + descriptors) and append its predictions as a fourth column. Settings: iterations=500, learning_rate=0.08, depth=6, loss_function='RMSE', rsm=0.1, thread_count=8, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, allow_writing_files=False. Change the oof array width in fit_predict from 3 to 4. To stay inside the 10-minute limit (base_predict runs 6 times per fit, 90 times per job), reduce RF n_estimators from 200 to 150 if needed, and lower CatBoost iterations to 300 if a job runs over 8 minutes.

items.title: Kernel SVR alongside KRR on the same kernel
items.spec: The KRR learner minimises squared error, while the metric is MAE. In base_predict, after the KRR grid has chosen (lam, wr), reuse the already computed combined Gram matrix K = Ta + wr * Ra to fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) on (K, ya - mu), and predict on the test kernel tanimoto(Fb, Fa) + wr * rbf(Zb, Za). Return its predictions as an extra fourth column and widen the oof array in fit_predict to 4. The positive Ridge meta-learner decides how much weight it gets. No extra grid search for the SVR.

items.title: MAE-optimal non-negative stacking weights
items.spec: Replace the Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True) meta-learner with weights that minimise out-of-fold mean absolute error directly. Parametrise as intercept + sum_i w_i * oof_i with w_i >= 0, and solve with scipy.optimize.minimize (method='L-BFGS-B' on a smooth approximation such as the pseudo-Huber loss with delta=0.05, bounds (0, None) for the weights, starting from the Ridge solution). Apply the same weights and intercept to base_te. Keep it to about 10 lines; base learners stay unchanged.

items.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion count features for trees
items.spec: Add two more fingerprint blocks to the feature matrix used by RF and LightGBM: hashed atom-pair counts and hashed topological-torsion counts, each 1024 wide, from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=1024) with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Insert them AFTER the descriptor block or otherwise keep the indexing correct: the code assumes the first N_BITS columns are ECFP and that descriptors start at column 2*N_BITS, so the simplest route is to build X as [ecfp, fcfp, descriptors, atompair, torsion] and change the descriptor slice in base_predict to Xa[:, 2*N_BITS : 2*N_BITS + n_desc], with n_desc = len(Descriptors._descList). The Tanimoto kernel stays on ECFP only.

items.title: Replace random forest with ExtraTrees
items.spec: In base_predict, swap RandomForestRegressor for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). Extra-trees are typically stronger than RF on sparse binary fingerprints, are faster to fit, and their errors are less correlated with the boosted model, which helps the stack. Remove the unused RandomForestRegressor import and the unused module constants N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF. Nothing else changes.

items.title: MLP ensemble on standardized descriptors as extra base learner
items.spec: Add a neural base learner for diversity. In base_predict, reuse the standardised descriptor matrices Za/Zb (already computed for the RBF kernel) concatenated with the FCFP bit block (columns N_BITS:2*N_BITS of Xa/Xb), and fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 128), alpha=1.0, learning_rate_init=1e-3, batch_size=64, max_iter=60, early_stopping=False, random_state=seed + k) for k in 0..2 on the target ya - mu; average the three predictions and add mu back. Return it as a fourth column and widen oof in fit_predict to 4. If the job exceeds about 8 minutes, drop to 2 networks or max_iter=40.

items.title: Tune LightGBM capacity: slower rate, more rounds, sparser columns
items.spec: The LightGBM learner uses a fixed (31 leaves, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.2) config at learning_rate 0.03 for 600 rounds, which is likely under-trained for about 2700 molecules with over 2200 features. Change to learning_rate=0.02 with N_ROUNDS=1500, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=5, feature_fraction=0.15, and add max_bin=63 to keep the runtime close to the current one. Also delete the dead constants N_CONFIGS and LGB_GRID, and simplify lgb_params to take only the seed. Keep the objective and all other learners unchanged, so the effect is attributable to capacity alone.
